name: Sled Start Isometric Drive

swap: Wall Lean Iso Hold (3s) + Plate Push (10m)

manual.why: Overcoming massive friction from a dead stop requires extreme trunk rigidity.
manual.cue: If your core collapses, the sled stops.

execution: Heavy Seated Cable Row (slow eccentric) + Backward Band-Resisted Drag
swap: Heavy DB Row + Reverse Sled Drag

name: Fatigue Lunge Yielding
execution: Heavy Dumbbell Squat (DBs at sides, 6 reps, 3s lower) + Immediate DB Walking Lunges (10m, same DBs)
swap: Heavy DB Split Squat + Sandbag Walking Lunge

manual.why: Forces the athlete to maintain posture and eccentric control when the quads are saturated with lactate.
manual.cue: Anyone can lunge when fresh. We train perfect lunges when your legs feel like lead.

name: Compromised Grip Carry
execution: Heavy Trap Bar Deadlift (5 reps) + Immediate Heavy DB Farmer's Walk (20m)
swap: DB RDLs + Heavy KB Suitcase Carry

manual.why: Fatiguing the CNS and forearms mimics entering the carry station under total systemic fatigue.
manual.cue: Your grip is going to fail on race day. We train it to hold on when fried.

swap: Landmine Push Press + Banded Squat Jumps

name: Broad Jump Lactate Tolerance

swap: S-Bike Sprint + Squat Jumps

name: Sled Drive to Run-Out
focus: Horizontal Drive to Upright Run Transition
execution: Heavy Sled Push (10m) + Immediate Upright 20m Run (tall posture, relaxed race pace)
swap: Heavy Wall Lean Drive (5s hold) + 20m Run

manual.cue: Push low, pop tall, run tall.

name: Burpee Broad Jump Landing Quality
execution: Burpee (chest to floor) + Immediate Max Broad Jump to Two-Foot Stick (2s), walk back, 5 reps
swap: Chest-to-Floor Push-Up + Squat Jump to Two-Foot Stick

manual.why: The BBJ station repeats a floor-to-jump transition hundreds of times.
manual.cue: Chest down, pop up, jump long, land quiet.

name: Grip-to-Legs Transition

swap: DB Farmer's Walk (20m) + Goblet DB Walking Lunge (10m)

manual.why: The carry station is followed by the sandbag lunges, with the hands and forearms already fried.
manual.cue: Drop the weights, scoop the bag, stay tall, and step long.

swap: DB Farmer's Walk (20m) + Goblet DB Walking Lunge (10m)

manual.why: The carry station is followed by the sandbag lunges, with the hands and forearms already fried. || TAG CLEANUP, NEEDS A COACH CALL. The 'Kettlebell' tag was flagged dead because the execution says only 'Heavy Farmer's Carry' and never names the implement, while the swap already specifies dumbbells. Kettlebells are proposed on that basis: if the primary carry were also dumbbells, the swap would reuse the primary's implement and fail filter 3, which is the exact problem swap_equipment exists to surface. name: Sled Start Isometric Drive
execution: Heavy Sled Isometric Lean (3s, arms locked, 45 degree angle) + Immediate Heavy Sled Push (10m)
swap: Band-Anchored Lean Iso Hold (3s) + Band-Resisted Sprint (10m)

manual.why: Overcoming massive friction from a dead stop requires extreme trunk rigidity. || FILTER 3 INVERSION FIX. The original audit rationale is not recorded for id 51, so this is re-derived - but it is a mechanical finding, not a judgement call. equipment was tagged ['Sled', 'Wall', 'Plate'] when only the Sled appears in the execution; Wall and Plate are swap-only and were folded in, which is the legacy pattern AGENTS.md tells us to split. Once split honestly the inversion check fires on its own: one Sled for the primary against Wall PLUS Plate for the swap, so the fallback needs two implements and two stations to the default's one, and needs a wall and plates on top of whatever was already unavailable. That is condition A of the check, and it is exactly the failure mode AGENTS.md describes - a swap that solves nothing for the athlete whose sled is booked. The swap is now a single common-tier Band, one implement against one, which passes both conditions. Honest trade: a band-resisted sprint is far lighter than a heavy sled push, so the swap preserves the trunk-rigidity-under-load quality and the static-to-dynamic contrast at lower intensity. The primary is untouched - static lean into an immediate push on the same implement is a clean flow, and a sled needs no rack.
manual.cue: If your core collapses, the sled stops.

name: Sled Pull Backward Lean
focus: Upper Body Pull & Posterior Chain Drag
execution: Heavy Seated Cable Row (slow eccentric) + Backward Band-Resisted Drag
swap: Heavy DB Row + Reverse Sled Drag

manual.why: MECHANICAL DATA FIX - NO COACHING CHANGE. This record had the same folding defect as ids 30, 51 and 60: ['Dumbbell', 'Sled'] was used only in the swap text but was folded into `equipment` instead of `swap_equipment`. The tag was not dead - it genuinely names an implement this drill needs - so it never tripped the dead-tag warning; it just sat in the wrong field, where it made the primary look like it needed a scarce tool it does not use, and it hid the split from filter 3 review. Correct split: `equipment` ['Cable', 'Band', 'Dumbbell', 'Sled'] -> ['Cable', 'Band'], `swap_equipment` None -> ['Dumbbell', 'Sled']. Execution, swap, focus, loading and rest are unchanged - the movement is identical and only the tag fields differ. Checked against the inversion check before writing: the swap needs 1 implement against the primary's 2, and the swap's implement is common-tier, so it is not trading a scarce tool for a cheaper one. Filter 3 intent is unchanged and now legible: comparing the two lists shows the swap drops the scarce implement, which is what the folded version could not express.
manual.cue: Upper Body Pull & Posterior Chain Drag
